Shell.//: The desktop shell only. A key is named by the character it types, with optional Ctrl+/Shift+/Alt+/Win+ prefixes; it is resolved through the keyboard layout in front at the time. These keys are watched, not claimed -- they still type normally everywhere else, which also means typing one triggers Morrow.
Shell.//MaxHeight: The overlay grows upward past Height to fit a long reply and stops here. A watermark is not a transcript; the conversation window is one click away.

Dictation.//: Speech to text, on the CPU, in the shell's own process. The microphone is the one input that carries the room, so it never leaves the machine whatever the tier says. Weights are not committed: run scripts/get-whisper-model.ps1 once. Without them the voice key says so in the tray and records nothing.
Dictation.//ModelPath: Multilingual base, not base.en -- two languages are spoken here. Any single ggml*.bin in that directory is used if this name is missing, so a bigger download needs no edit.
Dictation.//Vocabulary: Handed to whisper before every take as an initial prompt. Proper nouns only, and few: it moves the odds towards words the decoder has no reason to expect. Her own name is the one that matters -- add household names here too. Empty switches the bias off.
Dictation.//Language: Pinned by default -- 'auto' let a take now and then land in the wrong language with no way back mid-conversation. The tray's Language menu (en/fr/es/de) writes here at runtime.
Dictation.//HoldMs: How long the key must be down before the microphone opens. The voice key is a hyphen that still types, so a typed one must not record.
Dictation.//MaxSeconds: Ceiling on one take, so a key held down by a game or a book does not record the afternoon.
Dictation.//SilenceFloor: Peak amplitude under which the take is called silence. Whisper asked to transcribe a quiet room answers with words nobody said.

Screen.//: One shot of the primary screen at the moment the voice key arms -- what the person was looking at when they decided to ask, which is often gone by the time the sentence ends. Every take is captured whether or not the question turns out to be about the screen; the folder is flat, sorts chronologically and is the source of truth if any of this is rebuilt. Nothing is sent anywhere by taking it. Enabled false means no capture ever happens.
Screen.//MaxEdge: Long edge in pixels. 2048 is where the vendor's own high-detail resize lands anyway, so anything larger is bytes thrown away; a 4K screen becomes about 2,800 input tokens. Lower saves with the square -- 512 is 173 tokens -- and is also where on-screen text stops being legible, which happens below about 1024.

_sight: The screenshot the shell took when the voice key armed, looked at by a model. Two switches stand between the screen and the network: this Enabled, and a Substrates:Agents:Sight entry pointing at a provider with eyes. Neither on means the shot is still taken and still read by the machine's own OCR, which never leaves the machine -- she knows what the screen says and not what it looks like, which is the Free tier.

Sight.//CloserEnabled: Whether high detail is ever paid for. A cost switch: off, the escalation is never bought and a reading drops to Detail instead of being refused. On here, off on Budget; Free has no eyes at all, because its Sight entry never calls a substrate.
Sight.//Detail: Low fits the screen into 512px for 173 tokens: enough to say what is on screen, nowhere near enough to read a label -- the local OCR covers that half for nothing. High resizes to 2048 for sixteen times the price. Low is the default on every tier, because a cheap look every turn plus a close look on the turns that ask for one is cheaper than always paying, until nine turns in ten need the close one.
Sight.//CollectMs: The look starts when the microphone opens and usually finishes while the person is still talking, so this ceiling is for the unusual case. Kept well under Governance:BundleTimeoutMs so a slow look costs a blind turn rather than a late reply.
Sight.//CloserPhrases: What buys the close look. Config because two languages are spoken here and a list of English verbs would leave half the questions about the screen on the cheap pass. Matched as substrings, case-insensitively.
Sight.//ReadPhrases: Read it to me, as against have a look. A reading goes straight past Intent and is spoken at whatever length the screen takes, because someone who cannot see their screen is owed the screen and not a summary of it. Kept narrow on purpose: a question mistaken for a reading spends the whole turn reciting a screen nobody asked about.

_discord: Off until a bot is actually registered and invited to a server -- DefaultChannelId and the token env var below are both empty on purpose. DiscordToolkit no-ops with a clear error rather than throwing when either is unset.
_energy: MaxHours is the ceiling M, in hours of regen. AnnualBudgetUsd is R, and the only number that sets annual exposure.
_maintenance: Not a tier. The rebuild runs whichever tier booted -- a Free boot still repairs its memory with the good model, because a tier is what the persona thinks with and this is not the persona thinking. Replaces lists the model ids whose extractions may be thrown away; rows naming no model at all are always included. Leave Rebuild out entirely to switch the pass off.

openai.//MaxTokensField: OpenAI retired max_tokens on its reasoning models and answers 400 to it, saying nothing about which parameter it disliked. Every other endpoint here still takes the old name.
